reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered ALFWorld measurement of what fraction of a procedural memory bank's task-type-specific advantage is already held by a GEPA instruction optimized on the identical episodes, identified by crossing instruction provenance with bank provenance over a fetch-and-place vs appliance-operate split of the six task types, and reported as a scale-free absorbed share A = 1 - Inner(I_own)/Inner(I_oth) with a co-primary neutral-denominator twin A0.
reviews.closest_prior_work: AutoManual (arXiv 2405.16247) is the most dangerous, and the proposal concedes it only after a reviewer supplied it: it builds rules from ALFWorld interaction and compiles them into a single markdown manual that replaces per-episode experience lookup, in this exact environment. Together with AutoGuide (2403.08978) it already establishes both halves of the framing - episodic experience can be rewritten as instruction text, and a compiled manual competes with retrieval - so the title question 'is your agent's memory just an un-optimized prompt' is a 2024 question, and prediction 6 (row 11, compile-once) is a replication with token matching, as the proposal admits. ExpeL (2308.10144) removes the architectural distinction entirely by storing its memory as a prepended natural-language insights block, and EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) supplies the qualitative headline on shared trajectories. What survives is genuinely narrower than the title: labelling both containers by episode provenance, running the crossover, and putting a CI on the resulting ratio. That is identification-and-quantification on top of an accepted qualitative result, which is what the proposal itself says its worth is capped at.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory bar is explicitly A and A0 and 'nothing else', yet the rival that best explains a large A is left unthresholded and one gate biases the estimate. (a) Generic compression: if I_own is simply a better-specified instruction, a well-specified policy is less steerable by any injected block, so Inner(I_own) shrinks toward zero with zero content transfer. The proposal's answer is the multiplicative headroom floor A_h = 0.06-0.12 - which it concedes is 'a model, not a law' - plus Ladder T, and Ladder T's A_epi is explicitly demoted to descriptive because SE(A_epi) is approximately 0.30. So the single number the paper is named for has no thresholded control against its own leading alternative. Worse, a generic loss of prompt-steerability shrinks help(I_own) and |off(I_own)| together, which lands in Rule M's 'otherwise mixed' bucket and therefore blocks nothing. (b) Rule M contradicts the bar: 'absorption is claimed only if the help term carries >= 2/3 of Delta-Inner' cannot coexist with 'Both must pass; nothing else gates the confirmatory claim.' One of those sentences has to go, and which one goes changes the paper. (c) Selection on the denominator: G6 requires Inner(I_oth) >= 5pt and Inner(I0*) >= 5pt 'on S_test', the same 1,200 games from which A and A0 are computed. A ratio conditioned on its own denominator exceeding a floor measured in the same sample is biased upward exactly in the hypothesis's direction, and the 90% one-sided bootstrap lower bound does not have nominal coverage under that rule. G3 is correctly on S_dev2; G6 is not, and nothing in Measurement and Noise Control addresses the conditioning. (d) The modal outcome is a branch, not the endpoint: G3 demands a 9pt type-specific advantage, which by the proposal's own algebra requires off(I0*) <= -4pt, i.e. that a bank built from pick_and_place / pick_two / look_in_light actively harms on clean / cool / heat games by four points, even though all six types share navigation, goto, take, open and put and the off-type bank still teaches all of it. The proposal calls G3 'deliberately a coin flip'; a reviewer will read that as roughly even odds that 990,000 calls buy a type-generic finding instead of the paper.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Promote I_type - the hand-written instruction given only the three type names and their canonical skeleton, zero episodes - to Tier 0 and treat it as a third level reference. At approximately 25,500 calls it is 2.5% of the budget and it is now the only cheap arm that separates 'absorbed these episodes' from 'knows which three task types are coming', because A_epi has been demoted and row 17's B'_own answers the bank-side question, not the instruction-side one (the proposal concedes exactly this in risk 26). Pay for it by cutting row 12 (J) to one seed or dropping the 25% arm of row 9. 2) Move G6's denominator floor off S_test onto S_dev2, as G3 already is, or reserve an independent slice for it, and report by simulation how much the conditioning inflates A under the pre-registered rule. 3) Decide Rule M's status in writing: either fold the >= 2/3 help-share into the intersection-union rule alongside A and A0, or stop saying absorption is 'claimed only if' it holds. 4) Fund row 4 at row-2 scale (or drop A_all, M_shuf, or one J seed to pay for it) so the study's central rival explanation has a thresholded test rather than a CI that is twice too wide. 5) Report absorption of the total bank gain g(I, B_own) - g(I, M0) as a co-reported endpoint, not only the type-specific Inner: the title, the abstract's rhetoric and the practical recommendation are all about the former, while the confirmatory number is about a restricted slice. 6) Run pre-freeze obligations (1) and (2) before submission rather than before the freeze - as written, novelty is conditional on searches that have never been executed.
reviews.missing_baseline: I_type at Tier 0 - a hand-written instruction given only the three task-type names and their canonical skeleton, no episodes. It is currently Tier 1 and refused with the reason that 'its decisive role was interpreting a branch that is no longer a decision rule', but that reasoning inverted once A_epi stopped being thresholded: without it, an A of 0.7 is equally consistent with 'the optimizer absorbed these 300 episodes' and 'any text naming the three upcoming task types kills the on-type bank's edge', and the paper cannot tell a reviewer which. Second omission a reviewer will demand: the raw long-context trajectory dump (R_raw / M_all) read at I_own, also Tier 1. EvoMemBench-style results that long-context baselines stay competitive against 15 memory methods are cited in the proposal's own Related Work, so a reviewer will ask why the cheapest rival container - just paste the episodes - never appears in the confirmatory grid while a distractor control, a shuffled-bank control and three denominators do.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually disciplined in form - dated scans (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), named verification channels, an explicit statement that arXiv is unreachable from the node, and up-front concession of EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) and ExpeL (2308.10144) rather than burial - and I can name no preprint that makes this exact absorbed-share claim. But the check does not establish novelty, and the proposal says so itself. First, the one search that would establish the novelty actually claimed - held-out-episode and data-provenance crossovers in the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures - is pre-freeze obligation (1) and its status is stated as UNRUN and freeze-blocking. An unrun search behind the load-bearing claim is a weakness, not a neutral. Second, obligation (2), the appendix of arXiv 2608.14036, is named by the authors as the live collision that would gut prediction 6 and is unopened. Third, the scan's recall is demonstrably poor exactly where this framing originates: it missed AutoManual (2405.16247, NeurIPS 2024) and AutoGuide (2403.08978), both pre-2026, both in ALFWorld, both rewriting episodic experience as instruction text, and both had to be supplied by a reviewer. A scan weighted to the last six months cannot certify novelty for an idea whose ancestors are from 2023-2024, and the promised pre-2026 re-sweep is also unrun. Fourth, verification depth: only EvoAgentBench was read from a PDF, and that PDF was PI-supplied; every other 2026 ID rests on a single web-snippet channel, and the load-bearing 'confirmed absent from the paper' claims for competitors are asserted from abstracts. My own knowledge does not extend past mid-2026, so I can verify neither the existence nor the content of the majority of the cited IDs, which means the claim that no combined optimizer-plus-memory provenance manipulation exists anywhere is currently unfalsified rather than checked.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A task-type provenance crossover in ALFWorld that labels a retrieved memory bank and a GEPA-optimized instruction by the episodes that built each, and reports as a scale-free ratio with a CI the fraction of the bank's task-type-specific advantage that the same-episode instruction already holds.
reviews.closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144) threatens novelty more than the proposal admits. ExpeL runs on ALFWorld, distills training episodes into a natural-language insights block prepended to the prompt, AND retrieves successful trajectories — and its own ablation removes the insight container and the retrieval container separately on the same training pool. That is the two-container comparison, in this exact environment, from the same episodes. The proposal cites ExpeL only for the framing concession ('memory as an instruction is not a framing we invented') and never engages with that ablation table; a reviewer who knows ExpeL will ask why the paper's Related Work treats it as a design-pattern precedent rather than as the nearest published measurement. Behind it, EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) supplies the qualitative headline (ReasoningBank +3.6 vs GEPA +1.2 on shared trajectories), MIPROv2 (2406.11695) the instruction-vs-demonstration split, and AutoManual (2405.16247) / AutoGuide (2403.08978) the compile-ALFWorld-experience-into-instruction-text result. What genuinely survives is narrow: provenance labelling of both containers and the interaction it identifies, the episode-disjoint controls, and a number with an interval. The proposal says this itself, and its self-assessed ceiling ('identification-and-quantification on top of an accepted qualitative claim') is the right one.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory estimand does not test the title, and can pass while the title's claim is false. A and A0 are built on Inner(I) = acc(I x B_own) - acc(I x B_oth), which isolates only the TYPE-SPECIFIC slice of the bank's value. Nothing in Inner touches the type-generic component. So A = 1.0 -- the instruction holds every scrap of type-specific content -- is fully compatible with the bank still adding 5+ points over no-memory at I_own, because the generic component was never in the numerator or the denominator. The proposal concedes the possibility in refutation route (vii), yet the bar is 'A and A0 only; nothing else gates the confirmatory claim', and the quantity that would decide the title, g(I_all, B_all), sits at n=800 under a +/-3pt TOST the proposal itself says is declarable 'only when the observed effect is within ~0.2pt of zero'. A paper can therefore report a passing absorbed share of 0.6 next to a real, unrefuted 4pt residual memory gain, and the answer to 'Is Your Agent's Memory Just an Un-Optimized Prompt?' is no. Second, and concretely: the co-primary A0 is presented as the neutral denominator but has the LARGEST headroom bias of the three, and that bias is never computed. G2 fixes acc(I_own x M0) - acc(I0* x M0) >= 3pt and the design expects a ~5pt gain from I0* to I_oth, so the I0*-to-I_own level gap is roughly 8-11pt; at the planned ~50% accuracy A_h(A0) = (l_own - l_0)/(1 - l_0) = 0.16-0.22, i.e. at or above the 0.2 lower-bound floor A0 must clear. Prediction 3's 'A_h <= 0.15' is defined only for the A denominator (l_own - l_oth)/(1 - l_oth), and the claim that the null replicates 'price the headroom floor into the decision' fails for A0 specifically, because the ladder-level null is computed between two ADJACENT Ladder-T rungs -- a small level gap -- not across the much larger I0*-to-I_own gap that A0 actually spans. The intersection-union test thus swaps a mis-specification bias for an uncomputed headroom bias, and the two endpoints share a numerator, so a numerator artifact moves both (risk 25 concedes exactly this).
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, none expensive. (1) Make the title's claim the confirmatory claim: promote g(I_own, B_own) = acc(I_own x B_own) - acc(I_own x M0) to the confirmatory family at n=1,200 (it is already free from rows 2 and 3), and pre-register the conjunction -- absorbed share above threshold AND residual memory gain equivalent to zero -- as the only outcome that supports 'memory is an un-optimized prompt'. A high A with a surviving memory gain should be pre-declared a 'type-specific content absorbed, generic content not' finding, with a different title, rather than a pass. (2) Compute and pre-register A_h separately for each of the three denominators, and add a null replicate that instantiates the I0*-to-I_own level gap (A between two instructions of that gap with no provenance difference), instead of relying on an adjacent-rung ladder null whose true value is a much smaller floor. (3) Take the frontier reflector the track budget explicitly offers (a few hundred dollars; the proposal costs its own reflection role at ~4,000 calls). The refusal is self-imposed, it makes G2 a 'live risk' by the proposal's own admission, and since a weaker reflector lowers A, it simultaneously biases toward the null AND shrinks the level gap the design is fighting -- taking the API removes the optimizer-failure branch and raises the chance G3's 9pt Inner is reachable at all. (4) Move R_raw / M_all read at I_own into Tier 0 and off the cut list.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. First and most damaging: the plain memory-vs-no-memory delta at the own-type optimized instruction, g(I_own, B_own) = acc(I_own x B_own) - acc(I_own x M0). It is computable for free from Tier-0 rows 2 and 3 at n=1,200, it is the quantity every memory paper the proposal cites actually reports, and it is thresholded nowhere, predicted nowhere, and absent from the confirmatory family -- while its weaker n=800 pooled cousin g(I_all, B_all) carries the entire deployment claim under a TOST margin the proposal admits is barely declarable. Second: the whole-bank long-context dump read at the optimized instruction (R_raw / M_all at I_own). EvoMemBench (2605.18421), which the proposal itself cites, reports long-context baselines staying competitive with fifteen memory methods; if simply pasting the bank at I_own matches retrieval, the container framing is about retrieval overhead rather than about instructions absorbing episodes. That arm is Tier 1 and fourth on the contingency cut list, i.e. likely never run.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually serious for a proposal -- dated scans (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), 15 queries over 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs, one competitor PDF read in full with a committed SHA256, a self-correction of a web snippet that misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6, and reinstatement of five IDs wrongly retracted in an earlier version. I credit that. But it does not establish novelty, for reasons the document itself supplies. All four pre-freeze obligations are declared UNRUN, including the freeze-blocking search of the contamination and data-attribution literatures for the provenance-crossover primitive on which the entire identification claim rests, and the named live collision -- the unopened appendix of arXiv 2608.14036 -- that would gut prediction 6. More telling than the unrun items is the scan's demonstrated failure mode: weighting to the last six months caused it to miss AutoManual (2405.16247, NeurIPS 2024) and AutoGuide (2403.08978), the two most on-point papers, in this exact environment, and they were supplied by a reviewer rather than found by the scan. A search process that has already missed the two nearest precedents once is evidence against the residual novelty claim, not neutral. Verification depth is also uneven: arXiv is unreachable from the node, so every 2026 ID except EvoAgentBench rests on a single web-snippet channel, and every 'confirmed absent from the paper' claim about a competitor other than EvoAgentBench is asserted from an abstract. On my own knowledge, the pre-cutoff IDs the argument leans on -- ExpeL 2308.10144, GEPA 2507.19457, MIPROv2 2406.11695, ReasoningBank 2509.25140, Memp 2508.06433, A-MEM 2502.12110, AutoManual, AutoGuide -- are real and accurately characterized, which is a genuine credibility signal for the unverifiable 2026 set. The collision the check misses is not a recent preprint at all: ExpeL's own ALFWorld ablation already separates a distilled-insight container from a retrieved-trajectory container built from the same training pool, and the check never treats it as a collision.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A crossover design in ALFWorld (the 'task-type provenance square') that labels both a procedural memory bank and a GEPA-optimized instruction by which task types' episodes produced them, and reports with a confidence interval the fraction of the bank's task-type-specific advantage that has already been absorbed by an instruction written from those same episodes.
reviews.closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144) is the work that most threatens novelty, and the proposal cites it five times without ever confronting the part that bites. ExpeL's learned artifact is a natural-language insights block distilled from training episodes and prepended to the prompt, and its published ablations already separate that block from the retrieved-trajectory demonstrations drawn from the same training pool, evaluated in ALFWorld among other environments. That is a version of 'what fraction of a retrieved-experience system's gain is already held by the instruction-shaped container built from the same episodes,' in this exact environment, already in print. The proposal concedes 'memory as an instruction is not a framing we invented' but then claims 'nobody has reported the number' -- a claim ExpeL's own ablation table substantially undercuts. What genuinely survives is narrower than the proposal presents: ExpeL fills both containers from one undifferentiated pool, so it never manipulates episode provenance and never runs the crossover, and its insights are not written by a reflective prompt optimizer. AutoManual (arXiv 2405.16247, NeurIPS 2024) independently pre-empts the compiled-block arm in ALFWorld (conceded in v5.2), and MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695) pre-empts the two-container ablation on a single training set. Stacked together, the residual contribution is the interaction estimand and the CI on it.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory endpoint does not measure the quantity the title and abstract claim, and the pre-registration contradicts itself about what licenses the claim. (1) Inner(I) = acc(I x B_own) - acc(I x B_oth) is the bank's task-type DISCRIMINABILITY, not its value. A >= 0.5 says the on-type-versus-off-type bank contrast roughly halves when the instruction is on-type; that is entirely compatible with the bank still adding, say, +6pt over no-memory at I_own. 'Is your agent's memory just an un-optimized prompt' requires g(I_own, B_own) to go to zero, and that quantity is never confirmatory: it appears only as row 5's g(I_all, B_all) under a +/-3pt TOST that the proposal itself computes is declarable only when the observed effect is within ~0.2pt of zero. The headline is therefore ridden on an endpoint that cannot establish it while the endpoint that could is pre-declared nearly unpassable. (2) The document double-specifies its own decision rule. Experiments states, in bold, 'Both must pass; nothing else gates the confirmatory claim' for A and A0, while Rule M states 'absorption is claimed only if the help term carries >= 2/3 of DeltaInner,' and Prediction 7 restates Rule M as a required outcome. In the live case where A and A0 both clear threshold but the off term carries the shrinkage, the pre-registration says both that absorption is claimed and that the reading is distractor-robustness. A design whose entire pitch is that every decision rule is fixed in advance cannot leave its headline decision ambiguous. (3) The co-primary structure buys less than advertised. A is inflated by the mis-specification/repair channel the proposal admits; A0's denominator Inner(I0*) is measured at the short hand-written scaffold, so A0 is inflated by the generic context-competition mechanism the proposal itself cites (arXiv 2604.27003) -- a long, directive optimized instruction competes with ANY injected block regardless of provenance. An intersection-union test controls type-I error only if each marginal null is unbiased; here both marginals are biased toward passing, by different mechanisms, so requiring both to pass is not the protection it is presented as. (4) Self-conceded and decisive for the title: risk 26 admits the instruction-side episode-versus-type test (A_epi) is under-powered at SE ~= 0.30 and de-thresholded, and that its Tier-0 replacement (row 17, B'_own) answers a different question. So 'the same training episodes in two containers' -- the title's actual claim -- is not tested at power by any Tier-0 arm on the container the paper is named for.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Make the practitioner quantity confirmatory: pre-register the retention ratio R = g(I_own, B_own) / g(I0* , B_own) -- every term already exists at n = 1,200 in rows 1, 2 and 3, so it costs nothing -- and title the paper after whichever endpoint the design can actually establish rather than after one it cannot. 2) Promote I_type to Tier 0 (~25,500 calls, ~2 hours, ~2.5% of Tier 0). 3) Resolve the Rule M versus 'single operational bar' contradiction with an explicit truth table over the {A, A0, Rule M, Rule R} outcome space, so no post-hoc reading is available. 4) Use the resources the track actually offers: the brief specifies 4xA100 and a frontier API for the reflector role at a few hundred dollars, and the proposal restricts itself to two GPUs and asserts 'there is no API key on this node,' then justifies cutting the third optimizer seed, the coupling arm (row 13), the step control (row 15) and I_type by an 84-hour ceiling that is an artifact of using half the available hardware -- while G2 (optimizer must beat I0* by 3pt) is at risk mainly because the reflector is a local 32B. Restoring the stated resources removes most of the refusals and most of the G2 risk at once. 5) Run the freeze-blocking provenance-crossover search and report its results in the submission, not merely promise it before DESIGN.md, and add a numerical confrontation with ExpeL's insights-versus-retrieval ablation to Related Work. 6) Report the ALFWorld throughput measurement before claiming the compute plan, since the entire 60-84h figure is transferred from a 6-call-per-episode QA setting with far shorter prompts.
reviews.missing_baseline: I_type -- the hand-written instruction given only the three task-type names and their canonical skeleton, with no episodes at all. This is the rival explanation for the entire headline result: an optimized instruction that absorbed nothing episode-specific, and merely encodes which task family the held-out games belong to, would produce exactly the predicted shrinkage in Inner(I_own) versus Inner(I_oth). The proposal has already designed and hashed it, prices it at ~25,500 calls, and then demotes it to Tier 1 on the reasoning that 'its decisive role was interpreting a branch that is no longer a decision rule' -- while a 500-game graded planted control (row 9), an 800-game compile-once arm (row 11) whose novelty is explicitly disclaimed, and an 800-game joint-optimization arm stay at Tier 0. That ordering is indefensible: I_type is the cheapest arm in the design that can kill the paper's own interpretation. A reviewer will also demand the raw-context / long-context dump (R_raw, M_all) at Tier 0 rather than Tier 1, given that the proposal itself cites EvoMemBench and AutoMEM for the finding that naive long-context and flat-file baselines match engineered memory systems -- if a raw dump of the same episodes reproduces Inner, the distillation-and-retrieval container being 'absorbed' was never doing the work attributed to it.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is the most conscientious part of the submission in form -- dated scans, query counts, per-ID verification channels, a corrected PDF read of ReasoningBank's Qwen gain (+3.6, not +7), and unusually frank concessions that EvoAgentBench publishes the qualitative headline and that ExpeL already stores memory as a prepended instruction. Judged as evidence for novelty, however, it is thin exactly where it is load-bearing. All four pre-freeze obligations are reported as UNRUN, including the freeze-blocking one: the search for held-out-episode and data-provenance crossovers in the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures. That is the search that decides whether the identification primitive -- the sole surviving novelty claim after the concessions -- is new, and the proposal states plainly that its novelty claim is conditional on a search that has not happened. That is a weakness, not a neutral. The check's demonstrated recall is also poor by its own account: it was weighted to the last six months and missed two directly on-point ALFWorld precedents from 2024 (AutoManual 2405.16247, AutoGuide 2403.08978) that a reviewer had to supply, and the pre-2026 window has still not been re-swept. Because arXiv is unreachable from the node, every 2026-dated competitor except EvoAgentBench rests on a single web-search channel, and every 'confirmed absent from the paper' claim except that one is asserted from abstracts -- which is precisely the kind of claim that cannot be established from an abstract. From my own knowledge, the pre-2026 IDs cited (2308.10144 ExpeL, 2406.11695 MIPROv2, 2405.16247 AutoManual, 2403.08978 AutoGuide, 2507.19457 GEPA, 2509.25140 ReasoningBank, 2502.12110 A-MEM, 2508.06433 Memp) are real and characterized accurately, which is a point in the check's favour; I cannot verify any of the 26xx identifiers, and every 'nobody has done this' assertion depends on them. I know of no preprint that runs this exact provenance crossover between an optimized instruction and a memory bank. But ExpeL's own ablation already reports a version of the two-container split on the same training episodes in ALFWorld, the compiled-block arm is conceded as a replication of AutoManual, and the crossover primitive is conceded as not the proposal's own -- so the collision that matters is not a single unfound preprint but the cumulative one the check itself documents.
